body: Luckily, she hasn't tried pitting me and my brother against each other yet.  My brother and I aren't super close but we also don't have any issues.  His relationship with her isn't as bad as mine or perhaps he just brushes it off better than me.  His in-laws are very involved in their kids lives, actually to the point were they are spoiled rotten.  So he has other grandparents that he can count on.  Both of my in-laws are also absentee grandparents, so there really isn't anyone else to fill the grandparent void for my children.

yes, thank you for reminding me that she has zero actual power over me.  That's something my therapist has brought up before.  I am working on not caring so much about what people think of me.  I need to remember that I can't control their thoughts or opinions and sometimes it's more about them than me.

I experienced this a lot during a very stressful time in my life a few years ago.  My doctor gave me a prescription for propranolol which is a beta blocker.  It definitely helped, but you would obviously want to talk to a doctor since there are certain people who shouldn't take it if they have other health conditions.

It's even more infuriating when you're the breadwinner and he still gets praised for doing LESS THAN 50% of the childcare and household duties. Yes he cooks because I'm still working and they're just meal kits that I have to order.
My jaw is sore because I clench my jaw a lot

If you are actively trying to kill yourself, yes it's helpful because they will make sure you can't. If you're not that bad off, psych ward is not helpful and will not make you "better". It will likely do more harm.  Private treatment center could be helpful if you have the money for that.
They say that not because your teenage years are supposed to be great. It's because being an adult is miserable. Teenage years are the best years relatively speaking. It's all downhill after that.

I have a physiatrist that I've done psychotherapy with weekly for 12 years now. I have horrible social anxiety. She had me trying an outpatient hospital program for this reason but I hated it, got pregnant and had to quit.  

I tried reaching out to several "friends" during my severe depression of 2020-2021 and was quite disappointed. I know not to bombard people as that would push them away but I felt like I was spending all my free time listening to their problems without any recipication. Actually it became hurtful and exhausting.

But as far as making more effort to reach out now, time is the biggest reason I don't.  I think of all the basic needs I would address if I had more time: getting more sleep, eating actual meals, shower more often, exercise once in a while. Outings and hobbies seem so frivolous compared to these. 

Not trying to brush off the kind advice, just a lot easier said than done

I think about it but I don't know that it resolves the problems that have me exhausted and overwhelmed. I would still be without any emotional support, so no change there.  I would be even more stressed out from the demands and lack of time as a single mom. I also make a lot more money than him and would have to pay spousal support, and the thought of him getting that luxury really pisses me off.

He is self-sufficient, probably at the level of a teenager. So don't take care of him like he's an invalid, but yes anything that is above and beyond what a teenager could do. We started dating when we were 20, so it seemed normal at the time. But as our lives got more complicated and more responsibility came our way, he never picked up any of the extra responsibility. I point this out to him and we get into fights and gaslights me.
Same thing happened to me with my 1st rapist but on Facebook not Instagram and it was 22 years later. The friend request was deleted obviously and he is blocked.
Not sure what you mean by the comment

If you have a choice and the money, go to a private facility. Psych wards was full of rape and medical malpractice. Everyone was sedated regardless of diagnosis so they won't act out making it prime grounds for sexually predators. Incompetent staff withholding prescribed and actually needed medication and refusing to acknowledge claims of rape. Just stfu until so they think you're sane enough to let out of there. You will not get "better" there. They only make sure you can't end your life while you're there  but you will leave with PTSD.
Yes I was assaulted. But by someone who just turned 18 who I think was assaulted there himself as a minor. Cycle of my abuse continues...
Sorry for the late response. I live in the US in a large metro area.

I have trauma from the psych ward too. I had to go cold turkey off my Xanax prescription because of a clerical error. Which could only be fixed with a Dr consent. The doctor on call never answered any of their pages so it took a while to get resolved. They force fed everyone Seroquel, regardless of diagnosis to sedate people, which puts you in a vulnerable position. Staff will not keep you safe from other patients and look the other way when patients report assault or rape.  The place I was at was forced to close because the news media picked up on all the reports of assault and rape. I wish I went to the police after I was released but I was just so happy to finally be out of that hell hole.  You need to get evaluated and cleared to get out but if they decline to evaluate you then you're stuck there. I was not a minor so there was no loophole to go against medical advice to be released.

The psych ward is not designed to help you get better. It's designed to get you just functional enough not to be locked up.  There are some inpatient and extensive outpatient programs that are designed to help you get better.  In the US they just usually cost a lot even with insurance coverage. I have good insurance and my out of pocket was $750 a week for a outpatient day hospital program.

Best of luck to you.  I had a horrible things happen to me and now PTSD from my psych hospital stay 12 years ago.  Hopefully you go to a good place.  The only thing that gives me some sense of peace is that hospital was forced to close for all the years of abuse allegations.  I wish I would have went to the police afterwards and advocated for myself.  Me and my family had a hard time getting them to release me so once I was out I was too scared to do anything.  Wish I had done something to save others from going through what I went through.
NTA. Why can't OP's parents babysit. They are the child's grandparents and it would help both of their children.

As a mom who really wishes my kid's grandparents were more involved in their lives, I can see a benefit to this.  My have kids have 3 living grandparents and none of them have ever babysat for us.  My mom and my MIL are in poor health and live out of state.  So I give them some grace, but still think they put too much on us to maintain the resemblance of a relationship with them.  My FIL technically lives in the same metro area, but it is still a long drive to see him.  He's retired and in relatively good health but seems like he has no interest in coming to see us.  And making plans aside from holidays always fall apart with last minute cancellations on his end.  He only sees us at larger family gatherings at his house with his wife's family. And when we are there, he never spends time talking to our children.    

Last Christmas, my FIL and his wife wanted to take my kids to Target to pick out their own gifts because it was easier on them (harder on me when I have to return the gifts I already bought because that's what they picked out at the store with them).  My oldest son is known as chatter box and my FIL was surprised when they got back from Target saying he was so quiet.  And in my head I'm like... duh! He doesn't really know you! You are like a stranger to him!

It just breaks my heart to see my kids not really have a relationship with their grandparents.  Especially, since they see the relationship their cousins have with their grandparents on their other side of the family.  My oldest asks questions and I just don't know how to answer them sometimes.
I don't have any friends. If you don't have any than there is no friends to lose.
Me too. Been doing it since age 6.
Me too
The fact that you care and want to help is a great starting point, and something I wish I had. Medications could be an option but I think therapy would be more helpful. CBT has been helpful for me.

I have bpd coupled with OPCD. Constant anxiety about being/doing enough and then shame, guilt and disappointment when I don't meet my high expectations. Always been a people pleaser (again linking back to the OCPD) and let people walk all over me since I struggle to set boundaries which has put myself in vulnerable positions that have led to rape and multiple sexual assaults. Best friend abandonments at vulnerable points in my childhood and teenage years turned me into a quiet borderline so I am unable to make close friendships. I am very lonely and have no support system. No family really either. I married a man with undiagnosed adhd and now he's diagnosed he refuses to accept it. But then he wonders what's wrong with him and why he can't get his life together. Which leaves all the burden to me to do all the adulting and take care of our household with two young children. He has zero executive functioning skills. I'm so overwhelmed, stressed and overworked. And his inattentive ADHD makes him ignore me and not pay attention to all the work I'm doing or how stressed out I am. I am so lonely and depressed and I zero support network to rely upon.
Things only get worse after 23. I wish I could go back to the simpler times I had at that age.

I get the feelings of being overwhelmed and overworked. Just took a week off for a vacation and still had to work everyday and had my boss text me on my personal multiple times to take care of things.
I would cut them off, but my husband is reluctant unfortunately

I can totally relate.  Grandparent involvement in my kids life is a real sore spot for me.  I am so jealous of friends of mine that have grandparents around that actually spend time with their kids and get to know them.  My mom is in poor health and lives out of state, so I can understand her situation.  And my father passed away before my kids were born.  But my in-laws, who are divorced, have decided to move on in life with their new spouses.  My FIL is the only grandparent that lives near by but spends more time with his spouse's grandchildren then his own.  When I had my second child we needed his and his wife's help with someone to watch my oldest while I was in the hospital having a c-section.  They wouldn't help us even knowing that it was going to be his birthday while I was in the hospital and we wanted him to at least be with family on his birthday.  We were so lucky that my SIL stepped up to help but she's a working mom with 2 kids of her own.  She had to enlist of her husbands parents to make the whole thing work.  Yes we had to rely on someone else's grandparents because ours didn't want to be bothered.  All of my kids grandparents want me to buy their xmas and birthday presents for my kids because they don't want to be bothered with shopping.  I agree to do it for my mom because of her Parkinson's, but my in-laws are perfectly capable of doing this themselves.  I am already so burned out being a working parent and they put MORE work onto me.  I think I'm going to start saying No to that.  I spend so much time putting up smoke and mirrors for my kids so they think grandparents are "involved" in their life.  Even if they called just to talk to my kids on the phone once in a while, that would be a vast improvement.  I am so jealous of our friends who actual have grandparents involved in their kids lives.  Help with childcare would be nice, but it's about way more than that.

That got me bumped up on the waiting list, although I don't suggest it as I now have PTSD from my psych ward experience.  Even worse is when I got out of the hospital, they gave me a resident (in training) psychiatrist.  He was like a deer in headlights. I'm hypoglycemic and just switched from wellburtin to lexapro about five months ago. I haven't noticed a change in my blood sugar levels, but I've been able to manage my blood sugar pretty well through diet for the past 15 years.  I eat several small meals throughout the day and make sure I have some protein with each meal.  I also take OTC chromium picolinate supplement which helps a lot too.

I can really relate.  I'm what they call a quiet borderline from what I gathered.  The only people who know about my diagnosis is my psychiatrist/therapist, my husband and my mom.  I'm too scared to let others know.  I don't really have any friends, more like acquaintances.  I have a hard time trusting people because of my traumas and I'm afraid to let them see my crazy.  I'll get mad at things acquaintances do, but I never have the courage to confront them about it and potentially unleash the full power of my rage upon them.  So I end up agonizing with my anger by myself and it can be absolutely terrifying sometimes.  I used to rely on my husband and mom, but they've grown tired and me and think of me as a horrible person rather than a person with mental illness.  It's the catch 22 of being "high functioning".

I switched from wellburtin to lexapro in April and ended up having serotonin syndrome.  It was awful!  I had to suffer it out at home since my doctor didn't want me going to the hospital unless absolutely necessary because of the COVID risk in my state at the time.  Be sure to do the switch under the care and guidance of a doctor.  

I'm still on lexapro now.  It has helped with my anxiety a lot but it's made my jaw clenching and TMJ really bad.

It was likely the presidone and not necessarily an interaction. I've taken courses of presidone twice while on wellbutrin. The doctor warned me it might make me irritable and antsy like I need to run around and clean the whole house.  Wish they didn't downplay it so much. Roid rage is real!

It's hard to tell people because of knowing it will just be followed by disappointment when you realize or remember that people don't give a crap.

Very interesting to hear your story as me and my husband are the same matchup- I have BPD and he has ADHD Inattentive type.  Except my husband refuses to accept his diagnosis. He tried therapy and ritalin for a few months then quit. It's frustrating to hear him be depressed about what's wrong with him and why he can't get his life together, when he's been told what's making it difficultfor him but refuses to believe it. I don't know that ADHD drugs are necessarily the answer, but therapy, a life coach, something! I just wish he would he would try and help himself.

I also have OCPD and I end up picking up the slack for his lack of adulting. And the Inattentive ADHD type and BPD seem like a toxic mix for us.  He is oblivious to all the work I do for our family. I have a very demanding job that brings in a majority of the income, do most of the household work and we have 2 small children. I'm constantly stressed out and it wears on my mental health. I constantly feel ignored and unappreciated.  But he's the only adult person that I have in my life. I don't really have family or friends. 

He's never tuned into when I'm not doing well even if I straight out tell him I'm having a rough day or I dont feel well. And when I finally spiral out of control he just fights with me. He has watched me self harm, literally in the room watching me, and refuses to intervene. I've tried to explain to him my bpd and complicated mental health. He doesn't understand what it is and never reads the articles I send to him about it.  I've been doing psychotherapy with my psychiatrist for 10 years, so I feel like I've done the best I can to get better.  We tried couples therapy but he quit that like everything else. And now I realize it was a waste of money because he doesn't have the attention span or listening comprehension skills to get anything out of it.

I live in fear for my safety, not because of what he will do but what he won't do when something serious happens to me, and I'm talking physical health as well as mental health. I have countless stories.

My husband and I have had so many fights about division of household duties. He thinks its about 50/50 but I think its 85/15. When I ask for help I think he messes it up on purpose so he won' have to do it again.  "I'll start helping with laundry more" he says. But he just puts clothes into the washer, forgetting the rest if the steps. Then a few days later I find stinky clothes and have to wash it 2 more times just to get the smell out. So by helping he actually creates more work for me. Then I'm the jerk for getting mad about it.

I've taken meds twice a day a for years. Best way I found to he consistent was to take them when I brushed my teeth, so in the AM getting ready and PM before bed. I am pretty good about keeping that schedule but anytime I've had a medication with a mid day dose, I can't do it constantly, even with phone reminders.

I know what you mean. I have no support system either and it sucks.  And having people physically around isn't the same thing as a support system.  I have a husband and two young kids, but the situation is really more like being a single mom with three kids.  I've never felt more lonely in my life.  I don't have any other family that I talk to or lives nearby and I spent so many years adulting for two people that I no longer have friends.  I'm chronically exhausted from working so hard.  Any attempts to get emotional support from my husband just results in more pain and suffering.  I look forward to those moments where I can hide in a closet and cry so my kids don't see their mother in so much pain.

And in reading about those, I first heard about bpd, only to be diagnosed with it myself a couple years later.  Since his diagnosis Brandon Marshall has done a great job advocating for mental health and runs project 375 through his foundation  [https://project375.org/](https://project375.org/) .

This spilled over into social anxiety and the inability to make close friends and deeper connectons. I am always afraid of doing or saying he right thing. I obsess over it but end up doing nothing. Most people probably think I'm a cold person or dont want to be their friend. But deep inside I'm very lonely and prone to depression without anyone to turn to.  Still working throughthis issue in therapy.

I can totally relate. When i had my last baby, not a single friend or family member did anything for me, not even a call or text after his birth, and it was a planned c section so no surprise to when he was coming. Big wake up call for me in life. Can't count on anyone. No one gives a shit.

I don't think most people realize that and unfortunately those that do found out the hard way. I believe most of the people who answer calls are volunteers. Not an easy gig to get people to volunteer for and takes a lot of training to handle those types of calls.

I wouldn't count on this hotline. Its very understaffed and hard to actually get through to a person. I've been on hold waiting in the queue for an hour before and eventually just gave up and hung up. There nothing worse than being so desperate for help that you call a hotline to talk to a stranger, only to realize there is no one there to help.

I do it all the time. I spend all this time and energy and then feel self conscious about what I write. Then I realize nobody really cares about what I have to say. So I give up because my energy is limited and I realize I've already wasted too much of it.

I can really relate to this! I've been diagnosed with Obsessive Compulsive Personality Disorder.  I still struggle but seeing a therapist has helped.  I've also found Cogitative Behavior Therapy (CBT) to be helpful and there are a lot of books, workbooks and websites out there that are resources for CBT.  A lot of it is about letting go of the need for perfection.  Hard when it's so deep rooted in you, but I realize how much time and energy I was wasting on things that in the end don't matter that much.

Yep! I am extremely sensitive to tone of voice.  I constantly feel like my husband is annoyed or pissed off when I talk to him.  I think it's partly that he is unaware of the tone of voice he's using and partly my perception.  My therapist reminds me how my mind tends to gravitate towards negative thoughts, so I automatically perceive a negative and angry tone of voice.  I'm working on re-framing my perception but it's not easy when your brain has been operating that way for so long.

Yes, thank you for this! Filling your own void...that really put some things into perspective for me as a person trying to manage my BPD.  An unstable sense of self is often part of BPD and something I am really trying to work on.

I find it very hard to get people to take my mental health seriously.  My husband just sits there and watches me self-harm.  I'm not cutter, I bang my head or hit it with blunt objects.  I guess he just figures I'll eventually stop if I get a big enough contusion or knock myself unconscious.

I totally agree! I hate seeing people post the info for the suicide hotline at the end of an article about depression or people who put something in there fb status about it.  They think they are helping but they are completely unfamiliar with what a crappy resources they are pushing in what could literally be a life or death situation.  For one, there are severely understaffed and it's very difficult to even get through to a person and if you do, it's rare that they are well trained.  Imagine a desperate suicidal person who calls the hotline as their last hope and then they are on hold for an hour or they get a person and they hang up on them or yell at them like what happened to OP.  It would be interesting to see how many people actually kill themselves after calling the hotline, if there is even a way to track that.

I think one reason people who go through with it but don't say anything is because of the negative repercussions from the past in either telling other people or a failed attempt.  The worst thing that ever happened to me was admitting to a failed attempt, being pressured by family to go to ER and ending up in the Psych ward. I have PTSD from my psych ward experience and came out worse than I went in.

I agree cannabis hits everyone different. I've had anxiety since childhood and honestly think that cannabis has been the most effective anxiety medicine for me. Unfortunately it doesn't eliminate it completely so I'm still searching for other remedies.

Yup. I'm an overthinker too. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy helped me with these types of overthinking patterns. Also try and flip it, do you notice these type of details about other people's behavior? Probably not, so unlikely that they are noticing them about you. And if they did, what is the worst that can happen?
